title: Rate Lock Commitment Pricing Day, Locked Price and Expiration at Confirmation
content:
**Rule.** The lock desk confirms a Rate Lock Commitment within the product's confirmation period of business days after the request.

- **Pricing day.** The pricing day of a lock is the request's own business day only when the request was time-stamped no later than the lock desk cutoff time on a business day. A request time-stamped after the lock desk cutoff time, or on a Saturday, Sunday or federal public holiday, is priced on the opening rate sheet of the next business day, and that day becomes the lock date.
- **Locked price.** The locked price equals the request's rate-sheet price plus the lock's term price adjustment, rounded to the product's price rounding decimals.
- **Expiration.** The original expiration date and the current lock expiration date equal the lock date plus the lock term in calendar days. When that date falls on a Saturday, Sunday or federal public holiday, it rolls forward to the next business day at no cost. The lock expires at the lock expiration time on the lock expiration date.

### Pricing day by time stamp

| Request time stamp | Pricing day and lock date |
|---|---|
| A business day, at or before the cutoff | That same business day |
| A business day, after the cutoff | The next business day (opening rate sheet) |
| A Saturday, Sunday or federal public holiday | The next business day (opening rate sheet) |

### Worked example (hypothetical inputs)

A request is time-stamped on a Friday at 16:20, after a 16:00 cutoff. The rate-sheet price on the request is 0.250 points, and the lock is a 30-day term with a term price adjustment of 0.000 points. The lock is priced on Monday's opening rate sheet, assuming Monday is a business day, and Monday is the lock date. The locked price is 0.250 plus 0.000, which is 0.250 points. Thirty calendar days from that Monday falls on a Wednesday. If that Wednesday is a business day, it is both the original and the current expiration date.
